A Tale of Two Cities.text: After 18 years in the Bastille, Doctor Manette obsessively makes shoes, a skill he learned in prison.
A Tale of Two Cities.evidence: Lorry and Lucie find him in a small garret where he spends much of his time distractedly and obsessively making shoes – a skill he learned in prison. ... The novel tells the story of the French Doctor Manette, his 18-year-long imprisonment in the Bastille in Paris,

The Little Prince.text: Translated into 600 languages and dialects, it is the second most translated work ever, after the Bible.
The Little Prince.evidence: By November 2024, the book had been translated into 600 different languages and dialects worldwide. It became the second most translated work ever published, trailing only the Bible.

The Alchemist.text: Santiago travels to the Egyptian pyramids for treasure, only to find it was where he first dreamed of it.
The Alchemist.evidence: The story follows Santiago, a shepherd boy, in his journey across North Africa to the Egyptian pyramids after he dreams of finding treasure there. ... Santiago realises that the treasure he sought was where he had his original dream all along.

Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone.text: In the US it was published as Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone.
Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone.evidence: It was published in the United States the following year by Scholastic Corporation under the title Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone.

And Then There Were None.text: Agatha Christie called it the most difficult of her novels to write.

Dream of the Red Chamber.text: A whole field of study, Redology, is devoted to the novel.
Dream of the Red Chamber.evidence: Redology is the field of study devoted to the novel.

The Hobbit.text: Tolkien later revised it in the second edition to fit its sequel, The Lord of the Rings.
The Hobbit.evidence: As Tolkien's work progressed on its successor, The Lord of the Rings, he made retrospective accommodations for it in The Hobbit. These few but significant changes were integrated into the second edition.

Alice's Adventures in Wonderland.text: Carroll first told the story on 4 July 1862, while rowing up the river Isis with the three Liddell girls.

She: A History of Adventure.text: Its queen, Ayesha, rules as She-who-must-be-obeyed.
She: A History of Adventure.evidence: They encounter a native people led by a mysterious white queen named Ayesha (pronounced "Assha") who reigns as the all-powerful Hiya — in English, She-who-must-be-obeyed, or She.

The Da Vinci Code.text: It was Robert Langdon's second outing, after Angels & Demons in 2000.
